attempted_claim: Let d be a Hodge-special discriminant for Gushel-Mukai fourfolds failing condition (***) of Perry-Pertusi-Zhao, so a very general X in the divisor GM_d admits no Hodge-associated K3 surface even twisted and Ku(X) is not equivalent to Db(S) or Db(S,alpha) for any (twisted) K3 surface. Let X1 and X2 be very general smooth ordinary members of GM_d lying in distinct fibers of the period map, not generalized partners or duals, with Hodge-isometric Mukai lattices and identified Hochschild homology HH_*. Let Ku(Xi) be their Kuznetsov components. Decide by proof or disproof whether Ku(X1) is exact-equivalent to Ku(X2) by a Fourier-Mukai kernel inducing the given Hodge isometry and the HH_* identification. A complete answer is either such a kernel with HH and Hodge verification, exhibiting Fourier-Mukai partners across period fibers without any K3 transfer, or a rigorous obstruction from Hochschild cohomology or the Mukai Hodge structure proving Hodge-isometric but derived-inequivalent Kuznetsov components in the Brauer-free case.
decisive_failure: The EPW-Torelli obstruction argument could not be completed: corrected lattice counts give 0-dimensional forgetful fibers, canonical-class preservation under FM equivalences in the divisor case was unverified, and primary-source checks were rate-limited. No rigorous TARGET proof or disproof is claimed.
